transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. Can you tell me what’s been bothering you or what brings you in today?

I suppose... well, I haven't been feeling quite right lately. Um... I've been struggling a bit with eating. I guess what finally made me make an appointment is... well, after I eat too much, I've started going upstairs and... making myself throw up. Then I just try to act normal, like I'm just tidying up the kitchen or getting ready for bed. I just... I didn't know what else to do.

Can you tell me more about your eating habits? Specifically, do you ever feel like you're eating a very large amount of food in a short period, more than most people would eat in similar circumstances?

I suppose... yes. Um... when no one else is around, in the kitchen... I do. 

I might go through... well, whatever is there. Leftovers from a church supper... crackers, cheese, some cookies. Even things I've baked for my book club. I just... I end up eating it all in one sitting. It's... it's certainly far more than I would ever actually serve myself at a normal meal.
When you're eating these larger amounts of food, do you ever feel like you can't stop eating or that you're losing control over how much you're eating?

I suppose... yes. It's rather difficult to talk about. Um... once I start, it just feels like a switch flips. 

I'm almost... watching myself keep eating. Part of me is in my head saying, 'Linda, stop now,' but... my hands just keep reaching for more. I just... can't seem to stop them.
After these episodes of eating more than you intend to, do you ever make yourself vomit or do anything else to try to prevent gaining weight?

Yes... um, like I mentioned when I first came in. That's... that's really what finally made me realize I needed to say something to someone. 

After it happens, I... I go upstairs and make myself throw up. And then I just try to go back to normal, pretending I was just tidying up the kitchen or getting ready for bed. So... yes. That is what I do.
